review: 2:3–2:4 הֵפֵר אֶת־הַמָּוֶת / וְנָתַן חַיֵּי עַד — 2 Timothy 1:10 (הֵפֵר אֶת־הַמָּוֶת וְהֵאִיר חַיִּים); the Arabic أَبْطَلَ الْمَوْتَ … الْحَيَاةَ وَالْخُلُود is that verse, and Hebrew keeps the two clauses on two lines because the Arabic splits a word (أَنَا / رَ) across them and Hebrew cannot.
1:2 אַחֲרֵי שְׁלֹם הַפְּעֻלָּה — 'after the work was completed', for بَعْدَ إِكْمَالِ الْعَمَل; the noun פְּעֻלָּה is the biblical word for work done (Ps 64:10), and שָׁלֵם carries 'finished'.

5:2 רֵאשִׁית חֻפָּתֵנוּ — 'the beginning of our wedding-canopy', for بَدْءُ عُرْسِنَا الْمَجِيد; חֻפָּה is the glossary word for the marriage canopy, and the glory is carried by the next line's שִׁירָה rather than repeated.
6:4 בְּתִקְוַת הֶחָטְפֵנוּ — 'in the hope of our being snatched away', for لِرَجَاءِ الاِخْتِطَاف; the rapture noun has no biblical abstract, so the niphal infinitive carries it as in hymn 98.
4:2 מַפְגִּיעַ — Hebrews 7:25 (מַפְגִּיעַ בַּעֲדָם); the glossary fixes this participle for the Arabic شَافِعٌ ('interceding').
